title: How Much Does a Land Survey Cost? [2026 Data]
summary: A land survey can determine your property’s borders and settle property disputes. Learn how much a land survey costs and what can affect the price.

Cost Insights:


-


Professional land survey costs range from **$800** to **$5,500** per acre depending on your property size and terrain complexity.


-


Your land characteristics and the time of year directly impact your survey costs, with wooded or hilly terrain costing more than flat ground.


-


Account for research fees to access historical property records and potential travel charges if your surveyor's office is far from your land.


-


[Hiring a local land surveying professional](https://www.angi.com/nearme/land-surveying/) ensures your property boundaries are legally documented and prevents disputes with neighbors down the road.


In 2026, the national average cost for a land survey is **$2,300** , with most homeowners spending between **$800** and **$5,500** depending on property size, survey type, and terrain complexity. Costs can climb as high as **$25,000** for large or complex parcels with limited historical records.


## Land Survey Cost Factors: What Affects the Price?


Land survey costs vary widely because surveyors set their fees based on a combination of factors, from land characteristics and terrain to the availability of historical records. Understanding these variables helps you anticipate where your budget will land before you hire a pro.


### Size


Property size is one of the biggest drivers of land survey cost, with surveys starting at **$1,000** or less for parcels under an acre and rising to **$1,500** or more for a single acre depending on terrain complexity. Larger properties generally come with a lower cost per acre, so buying in bulk works in your favor here. The table below shows the different costs of a land survey by size:


Property Size (acres) Cost in 2026


1 $1,500–$3,500


5 $2,500–$4,400


10 $3,600–$6,500


25 $5,500–$12,000


50 $10,000–$25,000


### Labor


Land surveyors typically charge **$220 to $450 per hour** , with rates varying based on crew size and the overall scope of the project. Smaller surveys may need only one or two surveyors, while larger or more complex jobs require additional crew members. Research to obtain property records is billed separately, averaging **$85 to $160 per hour** .


### Terrain Type


The type of terrain on your property directly affects what you'll pay for a survey, with smooth, open pasture land costing less than wooded, hilly, or otherwise obstructed ground. Flat land is consistently less expensive to survey than mountainous terrain, so properties with complex topography should budget accordingly.


### Time of Year


The time of year can affect your land survey cost because challenging weather conditions make the work harder and slower. Dense foliage interferes with accurate measurements, while snow and ice can conceal critical evidence and create unsafe working conditions for the surveyor.


### Survey Type


The type of land survey you need is a key cost driver, since surveyors charge more when they must collect information beyond the standard required to establish property lines. The cost of your land survey can vary dramatically by type, as seen in the table below:


Type of Survey Costs in 2026


Boundary Survey $1,200–$5,500


Topographic Survey $2,000–$6,500


Mortgage Survey $1,500–$4,500


Fence Land Survey $1,000–$3,200


As-Built Survey $1,600–$3,800


ALTA Survey $2,500–$10,000


New Construction Survey $1,800–$6,500

### Availability of Parcel Information


When deed records are difficult to locate, surveyors charge extra for the investigative work required to track them down, particularly when that research cannot be completed online. You can avoid some of those additional charges by visiting the appropriate county offices yourself to obtain the necessary documents before the survey begins.


### Time


Rush jobs with tight deadlines cost more because land surveying requires significant preparation, planning, and scheduling to deliver accurate results. Last-minute requests are uncommon in this industry, so building lead time into your project timeline helps you avoid premium charges.


### Research


Surveys that require deep historical, topographical, or resource-based research can significantly increase your final cost, with charges running lower when records are accessible online and higher when surveyors must visit county offices in person to retrieve land deeds. Searching through county-specific filing systems takes time that surveyors bill for directly, and some companies employ dedicated research assistants to handle this work.


### **Travel Time**


Surveyors typically bill for travel time because employee pay begins the moment the crew leaves the office, covering trips to your property, records offices, or meetings with other land specialists. Mileage charges may only apply when the surveyor's office is a significant distance from your property, so proximity to a local firm can help keep this cost down.


### **Documentation**


Special maps or custom documentation beyond the standard survey report can add to your total cost of a land survey. If you need your surveyor to present findings to a zoning commission, local board, or legal team, expect to pay an additional hourly consulting rate for that time and expertise.


### **Boundary Adjustments**


A boundary adjustment is a legal process that alters the existing boundaries between two properties, requiring a formal application and the filing of survey results with the municipality for approval. Because both properties must be surveyed and the surveyor must prepare documentation for municipal filing, boundary adjustments carry extra costs beyond a standard land survey.

The last thing you want is to end up in a boundary dispute with your neighbor. Having a land survey readily available can prevent the need for legal proceedings and preserve your relationship.

### Location


Where your property is located affects what you'll pay for a survey, with rural areas generally costing less and metropolitan areas running higher. Costs for a land survey vary by state, as shown in the breakdown below:


Location Average Survey Cost in 2026

Ohio $900–$3,800


Colorado $1,200–$5,600


Florida $800–$3,600


## Land Survey Costs by Survey Type: How Does Type Affect Costs?


The type of survey plays a major role in total cost, as the required depth of work and detail vary significantly.


### Boundary Survey


A[boundary survey](https://www.angi.com/articles/land-survey-vs-boundary.htm) is the most basic land survey service, costing **$1,200 to $5,500** , and is commonly used when buying a home, starting new construction, or confirming property lines before installing a fence.


### Topographic Survey


If your property has natural features like streams, hills, or dense vegetation,[a topographic survey instead of a boundary survey](https://www.angi.com/articles/boundary-survey-vs-topographic.htm) gives you the detailed elevation and feature data needed to start a landscape plan. Budget **$2,000 to $6,500** for this service, in addition to any[landscape architect costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/landscape-architect-cost.htm) .


Angi Tip


If the terrain of your property is complex, getting a topographic survey done can be helpful. Topographic surveys help your pros identify all the natural features and elevations of your property to ensure they complete construction safely.


[Danny Smith](https://www.angi.com/articles/author/danny-smith)


Content Editor


### Mortgage Survey


A mortgage survey confirms the exact boundaries of a property as part of the financing process, and most pros charge **$1,500 to $4,500** for this service. Like a boundary survey, it ensures you know precisely what you're purchasing before closing.


### Fence Land Survey


Before installing a fence, a fence land survey confirms your property line so you stay on your own side, costing **$1,000 to $3,200** depending on your property's size and complexity.


### As-Built Survey


An as-built survey is a 3D survey used on large home or landscape construction projects to confirm how the completed build compares to the original plans, costing **$1,600 to $3,800** .


### New Construction Survey


New construction surveys cost **$1,800 to $6,500** and are compiled from multiple survey types, including boundary, staking, and topographical, to cover the full scope of a large build. They tend to fall toward the higher end of that range, given the volume of work involved, and you may also need this type of[survey for a plot plan](https://www.angi.com/articles/land-survey-vs-plot-plan.htm) of your entire property.


### ALTA Survey


An ALTA survey, performed to the standards of the American Land Title Association, is one of the most comprehensive survey types available, costing **$2,500 to $10,000** on average. These surveys are most commonly used by commercial property buyers,[homebuyers, or sellers who need a survey](https://www.angi.com/articles/who-pays-land-survey.htm) to resolve a title dispute.


## Why You Should Hire a Land Survey Pro


Hiring a professional to complete a land survey can get expensive quickly, sometimes costing as much as **$25,000** , with the entire cost going toward labor. While it might be tempting to save money and do the survey yourself, a DIY survey isn’t useful for establishing legal property lines, showing easement information, or getting approval for a construction project. Unless you want a survey to satisfy your own curiosity, you should hire a[land surveyor near you](https://www.angi.com/nearme/land-surveying/) .


### Here’s why it’s ideal to hire a professional land surveyor


Despite the potentially high cost, there are a few key benefits of hiring a pro that you won’t get from a DIY survey:


-


Only surveys from licensed professionals will satisfy legal requirements, so you’ll need a pro if you’re building a home, fence, or outbuilding, as well as for the sale or purchase of a property.


-


DIY surveys aren’t legal documents, so courthouses, attorneys, and real estate professionals won’t accept them as part of a real estate transaction.


-


It’s easy to make mistakes when sketching out a survey as a DIYer, and you may end up encroaching on neighboring properties or legal easements on your own land.


-


Professionals can use special tools and access historical documents to include information about underground utilities on your property, which are sometimes a key component of a survey.


## Land Survey Additional Costs: What Other Costs Should You Budget For?


A land survey is often just the starting point for a larger project, and the costs that follow depend on what you plan to build or design on your property.


-


[Building a fence](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-fence-installation-cost.htm) : Installing a fence costs an average of **$8 to $50 per linear foot** .


-


[Building a stone wall](https://www.angi.com/articles/stone-wall-cost.htm) : Constructing a stone wall costs **$2,250 to $7,800** on average.


-


[Adding a shed](https://www.angi.com/articles/what-would-be-cost-hire-6x8-metal-shed-assembly.htm) : Building a shed costs between **$350 and $4,000** for pre-fab options.


-


[Landscape design](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-hiring-landscape-designer-cost.htm) : Hiring a landscape designer averages between **$2,000 and $7,000** .


## How to Save Money on Land Survey Costs


While land surveys can come with a hefty price tag, there are some ways you can cut down on the total cost.


-


Plan ahead. By budgeting for other aspects of property ownership, like the[cost to clear land](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-clear-land.htm) or[land development costs,](https://www.angi.com/articles/site-development-costs.htm) you’ll have a better idea of what to look for regarding a land surveyor’s fees.


-


Know the type of survey you need. To reduce the chance of paying more for a type of survey that isn’t necessary, make sure you know the exact type you need before you start.


-


See if you can get a referral. Sometimes, if you’re working with a realtor or other contractors, you can get a discount when they refer you to a land surveyor.


-


Pick the right season. If your timeline is flexible, ask land surveyors what time of the year is less busy (and often less expensive) to cut costs.


Next Steps: Finalize Your Project With a Pro


-


Be prepared to discuss why you want the survey, as the type can affect costs and timelines.


-


Provide as much historical information as you can, as this can help your surveyor get a complete picture of your property.


-


If you’re hiring as part of a real estate transaction, double-check that the surveyor has no connection to the other party in the sale.


-


Ask your surveyor if you need to prep your land in any way, which could include clearing debris or ensuring access.

To prepare for a land survey, you must thoroughly check your land surveyor’s qualifications, reviews, and fees to align with your expectations. When it is time for the survey to be conducted, ensure that you have all your documents organized and available, know and mark your property lines, and inform your neighbors that the survey is happening.


To hire a land surveyor, you need to start by searching online for reputable professionals in your area. Here are a few steps to take when making a shortlist:


-


Browse land surveyor service website


-


Check credentials


-


Read customer reviews


-


Find their contact information


-


Call or email to inquire about more information


-


Ask how far they travel, if you’re some distance away


-


Find out how they charge for their services


-


Ask about schedule and turnaround times


-


Repeat these steps for one to two other services and compare pricing


If you or your mortgage lender think your land survey needs to be more accurate, double-check the survey report and get at least a second opinion from the original surveyor and an inspector, if possible. Although it’s unlikely, even reputable surveying companies can make mistakes. An inaccurate survey can cause problems down the road in the case of any property line disputes, so it’s best to resolve any inaccuracies as quickly as possible.


Land survey reports have a boatload of information relevant to several scenarios. Here are the types of information contained with a survey, though it depends on your chosen type of land survey. Exact boundaries and dimensions of a given property General topography, including both natural and artificial landmarks Location of utility fixtures, like water mains Confirmation of any easements or encroachments on a piece of property Assessment of land elevation to buy flood insurance Updated information to add to a pre-existing property map
